title: reduce-streaming-token-latency-kernel-scheduling-kv-cache-batching-backpressure-flush-cadence
author: Samir Gupta
description: Motivation: Streaming token generation latency has been a recurring customer pain point for low-latency chat experiences. This PR combines several complementary runtime optimizations targeting the token emission path: 1) tighten the token loop to remove unnecessary scheduling hops, 2) adaptive flush cadence for partial token batches under backpressure, 3) improved kernel scheduling heuristics to prioritize single-token fast-paths, 4) KV-cache warm path improvements and lock contention reduction, and 5) continuous batching tweaks to avoid head-of-line blocking. Goals: reduce per-token latency (median and p95) for streaming responses while preserving throughput and stability. Summary of changes: - Token loop: collapse async handoffs between stages; avoid double-queueing on hot path; introduce a light-weight in-memory fast-path when KV cache hit and single-token generation. - Flush cadence: adaptive flush timer that short-circuits when requests are idle and widens when batching benefits outweigh latency. Adds per-stream backlog estimator. - Backpressure: improved heuristics to detect downstream stalls and trigger flush or fallback to synchronous emission for that stream. - Kernel scheduling: new heuristic in scheduler to detect short-sequence single-token bursts and schedule on low-latency kernels (reduced kernel selection overhead). - KV cache: reduced lock scope and introduced per-shard read copy-on-write to minimize contention during concurrent streaming. - Continuous batching: reduce maximum coalescing window for low-latency streams; add tagging to avoid grouping latency-sensitive streams with large-batch throughput jobs. Testing and measurements: microbenchmarks and internal canary performed on prod-like clusters. Results: median per-token latency reduced from ~11.6ms to ~6.8ms (41% reduction) on small chat workloads; p95 improved from 33ms to 18ms; end-to-end sample chat latency reduced by ~20% under normal load. No regressions observed in throughput tests; unit and integration tests updated to cover edge cases. Checklist: - [x] Implementation and unit tests - [x] Integration tests and benchmarks - [x] Canary run and perf dashboard captured - [x] Documentation update (docs/perf/streaming_latency.md) - [x] No breaking API changes Rollout plan: Canary on Dedicated and Hosted region-us-east-1 for 72h, monitor streaming_metrics.token_emit_latency and increase rollout after stable 48h window. Related: ENG-4312 (token loop improvements), ENG-4350 (kernel scheduler tuning), SUP-1284 (customer incident related to stale flush cadence).

Samir Gupta: Answered — default set from canary telemetry (5ms under light load, up to 30ms under high throughput). Added comment and config flag 'streaming.low_latency_mode' with doc note.
Jordan Patel: Found a potential race in kv_cache_manager on shutdown path. Please add a safety check.
Samir Gupta: Added a guarded shutdown flag and a unit test to cover shutdown races.
Maya Rodriguez: Approving after minor nits fixed (naming and logging levels).

squash: reduce streaming token latency (token loop, flush cadence, backpressure, kernel scheduling, kv-cache, batching)

See ENG-4312, ENG-4350
release_notes: Significant reduction in streaming per-token latency (median ~41% reduction, p95 ~45% reduction) driven by token loop fast-path, adaptive flush cadence, kernel scheduling optimizations, KV cache contention reductions, and continuous batching tuning. No API changes. Rollout via canary. Monitor streaming_metrics.token_emit_latency.
notes: Canary: region us-east-1; 72h planned, promote after 48h stable window
Config knobs: streaming.adaptive_flush.enabled (true), streaming.low_latency_mode (true by default for small requests), batching.max_coalesce_window_ms (reduced for latency-sensitive)
